packageRules.description: Angular majors go through the update-angular skill: ng update's migrations across the packages and ~100 examples, the published peer ranges, and the docs, none of which a version bump does. Minors and patches still come through.

Architect is versioned 0.MMmm.p (Angular 22.2 is 0.2202), so semver calls its move to the next Angular major (0.2300) a minor, and the rule above doesn't catch it. The update-angular skill moves this bound up with each major.
Each Angular release accepts only some TypeScript minors (its typescript peer range), so a TypeScript minor on its own fails the install. The update-angular skill moves TypeScript with Angular.

@types/node's major is the Node version it types, and the packages support Node 22.12 and later (engines), so a newer major lets the type check pass code using an API Node 22 lacks. Majors move by hand.

package.json's packageManager names the npm this repository's lockfile is written with. A major changes how npm writes package-lock.json, so moving to one is a change of its own rather than a version bump (#599). Majors move by hand; patches still come through.

The Lynx iOS frameworks workflow runs CocoaPods on this Ruby, and it only runs when dispatched, so a Ruby major's checks on a pull request pass whether or not CocoaPods works on it (#596). Majors move by hand, the next time the frameworks are rebuilt.

The examples and packages/ui use Tailwind 3 on purpose: @lynx-js/tailwind-preset supports only Tailwind 3 (peer ^3.4.0), and with Tailwind 4 the build skips their tailwind.config.ts and they render unstyled though the build passes. examples/tailwind-4 covers Tailwind 4. Majors move by hand.

The rsbuild plugin hands rspack plugins a Compiler from @lynx-js/rspeedy, which pins an exact @rsbuild/core and so an @rspack/core minor (2.3 in rspeedy 0.19.0). The plugin types that Compiler with its own @rspack/core, so a newer minor installs a second copy and its declaration build fails on the two Compiler types (#506). Move it by hand when rspeedy moves. @rsbuild/core minors build fine (#505).
Each @ng-native package peers on the others at its exact version, so one moved alone fails the install (ERESOLVE). They move together.

The angular-lynx benchmark installs @blotch/* from tarballs that scripts/use-local-packages.mjs packs into .local-packages/, which is git-ignored, so Renovate never has them and every lockfile update there fails (#509). Its versions move by hand: copy the bumped entries from the root lockfile, or rerun the script after a root build.

The React Native benchmark apps keep their versions on purpose. apps/react-native is Software Mansion's app on the exact versions its original lockfile resolved, and apps/react-native-0.88 is that app moved to Expo SDK 58 with `npx expo install --fix`, which sets React Native and its libraries to the versions the SDK pins together: SDK 58 takes react-native-reanimated 4.7.1 with react-native-worklets 0.13.0, so 4.8.0 on its own fails the install (#566). CI doesn't build either app, so a bump's checks pass even when the app no longer installs. They move by redoing the Expo upgrade, as apps/react-native-0.88/README.md describes.

The angular-native benchmark is an Expo SDK 58 app too, and its React Native side is the set the SDK pins: react 19.3.0, react-native 0.88.1 and react-native-svg 15.16.0 exactly, with the expo modules and the other native libraries on their SDK 58 lines. Babel comes with the SDK too: Metro transforms the app with @expo/metro-config's own Babel 7, so @babel/core 8 at the root left the bundle byte for byte the same while the Babel 7 plugins hoisted beside it lost the core they peer on (#593). It's measured against apps/react-native-0.88, which the rule above holds still, so a bump here alone (#582, #583) would compare library versions as well as frameworks. These move with that app, by redoing the Expo upgrade (`npx expo install --fix`). Angular, @ng-native and the app's other dependencies still come through.

The Android template gets Lynx and PrimJS from Maven, but iOS gets them from our own XCFrameworks zip (packages/native/src/ios/frameworks.ts), which the Lynx iOS frameworks workflow builds and Renovate can't. An update on Android alone would put the two platforms on different Lynx versions, and 4.1.2 added list item animations (#590). So Lynx updates wait on the Dependency Dashboard: tick one to get the Android half, build the iOS zip for the same version as packages/native/README.md describes, and move both in that PR. Fresco and OkHttp wait with them: Lynx's image and fetch services are compiled against Fresco 2.3 and OkHttp 4, so those move when Lynx's services do. Media3 waits too: xelement-video 4.1.0 depends on media3-exoplayer and media3-ui 1.0.2, and the template's VideoUI reads that PlayerView, so a newer media3-common or media3-ui on its own would run ExoPlayer 1.0.2 against a newer media3-common, mixing versions that Media3 needs to match (#776, #777). They move to whatever media3 xelement-video depends on.

The react-lynx benchmark pins ReactLynx and its build tools exactly, and lynx-stack releases them together. As separate PRs each rewrote the app's lockfile, so the first to merge left the others in conflict (#938, #939, #941, #942), and while rspeedy lagged a release the React plugin nested a second web-core under itself. They come as one PR. Its README lists the exact versions, so update that line in the PR too.
